chunks.text: 72-year-old male, Unemployed, resident of Ang Mo Kio, Singapore.
Completed course of Ciprofloxacin for UTI (2018)
General Anesthesia with Epidural Anesthesia for Post-Operative Pain Management

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr./Ms./Mrs. [Patient's Name]. I'm [Provider's Name], the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your hip replacement surgery. I'd like to go through some questions to ensure your safety and comfort during the procedure. Is that alright with you?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, doctor. I'm ready. I want to make sure everything goes smoothly for my hip.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Let's start with your medical history. You've been diagnosed with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, osteoarthritis in both hips, and high cholesterol. Can you tell me a bit about how these conditions have been managed lately?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure, doctor. My blood pressure is okay with the Lisinopril, but sometimes it fluctuates a bit. My sugar levels have been under control with Metformin and Insulin Glargine. The hips have been really painful, that's why I'm having the surgery. And my cholesterol is managed with Atorvastatin.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for that. Now, regarding your medications, I see you're on Metformin, Atorvastatin, Lisinopril, Insulin Glargine, and Paracetamol as needed. Can you confirm if you are currently taking any blood-thinning medications, including those you may have stopped in the past year?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, yes. I was on Clopidogrel for a while, but I stopped it about six months ago. I had a minor cardiac event, and after completing the prescribed course, my doctor said I could stop. I'm not on any antiplatelet therapy now.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. It's important we know about all medications, even those you've stopped. You mentioned Paracetamol as needed; how often have you been taking it for your hip pain?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not too often, doctor. Maybe once or twice a week when the pain gets really bad. I try not to take it too much.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, about allergies. You've listed penicillin as an allergy. Can you describe the reaction you had?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, I had a rash and some swelling the last time I took penicillin. So I've been avoiding it since.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for that information. It's crucial for us to know. Now, regarding your surgery and anesthesia, we're planning for general anesthesia with an epidural for post-operative pain management. Have you had any previous anesthetics or surgeries that you'd like to share about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had a cataract surgery a few years back, and that was under local anesthesia. No other major surgeries, so this will be my first under general anesthesia.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, that's helpful. Lastly, can you confirm your NPO status? Have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, doctor. I've been fasting as instructed. Nothing since last night.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Thank you for going through all these questions with me. It's important we cover everything to ensure your safety. If you have any more questions or concerns, please don't hesitate to ask.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thank you, doctor. I feel more at ease now. I'm ready for the surgery.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:05] epidural needle in, ten milliliters of bupivacaine

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] hypotension, mean arterial pressure down to fifty five, gave one hundred milliliters fluid bolus

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:15] fentanyl twenty micrograms for breakthrough pain

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:30] normotension maintained, started iv fluids at one hundred twenty milliliters per hour

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm feeling a bit groggy, but okay lah. My left hip is sore, but not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Can you rate your pain for me on a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 is no pain and 10 is the worst pain?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'd say around 4 or 5. The epidural seems to be helping a lot.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Have you experienced any nausea or vomiting since the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No nausea, thank goodness. I was worried about that, but I feel fine.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. How about your breathing? Are you comfortable, or do you feel any shortness of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine. A bit of discomfort when I move, but I can breathe normally.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Do you remember anything from the operating room or immediately after surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really. I knew I was going in, and then I woke up here. So I guess the anesthesia worked well.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's expected with general anesthesia. Given your history of hypertension and diabetes, are you experiencing any unusual symptoms like dizziness, blurred vision, or chest discomfort?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing like that. Just the usual aches from the surgery.

72-year-old male undergoing elective left hip replacement under general anesthesia with epidural for post-operative pain management. Patient has a history of hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, osteoarthritis, and hyperlipidemia, all currently managed with medications. He also has a penicillin allergy with rash and swelling.

Patient's hypertension is managed with Lisinopril 10 mg once daily, though with occasional fluctuations. Type 2 diabetes is controlled with Metformin 500 mg once daily and Insulin Glargine 20 units once daily, with no recent hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia episodes. Hyperlipidemia is managed with Atorvastatin 20 mg once daily. The patient also takes Paracetamol 500 mg once or twice a week as needed for hip pain.

During surgery, the patient experienced hypotension with mean arterial pressure dropping to 55 mmHg at 08:10, which was followed by administration of fentanyl for breakthrough pain at 08:15. Normotension was maintained by 08:30 with IV fluids started at 120 milliliters per hour. The patient is currently NPO and has an ASA-PS II classification indicating mild systemic disease.

Monitor for signs of hypotension and ensure adequate fluid resuscitation. Watch for any signs of pain or discomfort that may require additional analgesia. Be aware of the patient's diabetes management needs, including potential for hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia. Ensure all medications are continued as scheduled, with attention to timing of insulin administration. Be vigilant for any allergic reactions, particularly related to penicillin, and avoid penicillin or related antibiotics.
Patient reports feeling a bit groggy but okay after surgery, with left hip soreness rated as 4 or 5 on a 0-10 pain scale.
Epidural anesthesia is providing effective post-operative pain management for the patient.
Patient denies experiencing any nausea or vomiting since the surgery.
Patient reports normal breathing with only a bit of discomfort when moving, but no shortness of breath.
Patient has no recollection of the operating room or immediately post-surgery period, indicating effective general anesthesia.
Patient denies any unusual symptoms such as dizziness, blurred vision, or chest discomfort, despite history of hypertension and diabetes.
General anesthesia with epidural for post-operative pain management was administered as planned.
